head: baf6cf5644f2a50a4bf737c1e03221308353095e
note: A new dashboard-v2 endpoint (POST dashboard_v2/query_batch/) that plans, cache-reads and runs up to 500 inline queries and streams NDJSON lines. Golden issues are the union of the real findings that review bots and the author posted on the first reviewed commit or on later commits, kept only when the defect was present at this head.

issues.summary: _error_line uses isinstance(error, _EXPOSED_ERRORS | InvalidTarget), but _EXPOSED_ERRORS is a tuple, so `tuple | type` raises TypeError whenever any item errors. In the request thread (planning/cache read error) the whole batch 500s; in a worker _run raises out of _work, no line is emitted, and the stream sends heartbeats forever while holding its batch slot.

The query_batch action sets @action(required_scopes=["query:read"]), and ScopeBasePermission returns the action's static scopes before calling dangerously_get_required_scopes, so the per-query product scopes are never enforced: a token with only query:read can run product-restricted kinds (MCPModelBreakdownQuery, MetricsQuery, ErrorTracking queries) that /query denies it.

_run and _refresh_in_background call process_query_dict with the default is_query_service=False and the endpoint never tags api_queries_budgeted, so personal-API-key queries through the batch skip /query's API-key handling: no chargeable/billing debit, no hourly API-queries byte budget, no per-team API concurrency limiter, no OFFSET block, and they get QUERY_ASYNC limits /query withholds from API keys.

QueryBatch._start calls copy_context() when the response is first iterated, after the view and CHQueries middleware have reset query tags and team scope, so every miss runs without access_method/user/API-key tags: a project-restricted token's managed-warehouse query rejected at planning is retried and accepted by the browser-session guard, API-key queries leave the API cluster and caps, query_log loses audit fields, and team-scoped model reads fail.

DashboardV2ViewSet does not implement /query's get_throttles, so query_batch gets only the generic per-request Burst/Sustained throttles while one request runs up to 500 queries; HogQLQueryThrottle, ClickHouse and API-queries throttles are bypassed, inflating a caller's query rate about 500x.

In _read_cache, an item whose plan_query_dict returns None (e.g. DatabaseSchemaQuery) or whose planning raises is appended to to_run without checking item.cache_only, so a cacheOnly=true target is executed with blocking computation instead of returning a miss, breaking the 'never runs' contract.

Hits are read with run_planned_query(CACHE_ONLY_NEVER_CALCULATE), a mode that skips the runner's requires_fresh_calculation() check, so queries /query always recomputes (system.information_schema / data-catalog status, retention-bound rows) are served stale from cache until expiry.

Stale swr hits call _refresh_in_background synchronously inside __init__ before the response is returned; each call rebuilds the runner via process_query_dict and re-reads the cache outside the prefetched read, so cached panels get nothing until every refresh is dispatched.

On client disconnect _close sends one cancel_query_on_cluster per active query id, but a worker that is still planning or waiting on a limiter has no SQL yet, and _cancelled is only checked on entry to _work, so the abandoned query is later submitted and runs to completion, holding its thread and the batch slot.

_read_cache decodes every hit separately and keeps each model_dump in self.ready with no dedupe and no byte budget, so 500 cacheOnly copies of one large cached result are decoded and held 500 times in one web worker before a byte streams (OOM risk for the pod).

Planning, S3/Redis prefetch and decoding all run in __init__ before any admission, and _start returns without taking a _batch_slots permit when there are no misses, so cache-only/all-hit batches have no concurrency bound and a slow reader holds its full ready buffer with no slot and no deadline.

Workers put finished results on unbounded Queue/asyncio.Queue without waiting for the consumer, so a slow-reading client lets up to 500 computed (possibly multi-MB) results accumulate in worker memory; there is no backpressure or byte limit on computed results.

The 8 _batch_slots are process-global with no per-organization or per-user share and are held until the stream finishes, with no stream lifetime; one tenant with a few stalled or slow-reading streams holds every slot and other teams' cache-miss batches get _BUSY.

The batch accepts ErrorTrackingFingerprintProjectionQuery and runs it through process_query_dict, skipping the ErrorTrackingFingerprintProjection burst/sustained throttles that QueryViewSet.get_throttles applies, so a user can run CPU-heavy t-SNE projections past the team's projection rate limit.

The view has no @monitor feature tag and the disconnect-cancel thread runs with no query tags, so batch misses are untagged (UntaggedQueryError under strict tagging, no feature in query_log) and the cancel lookup in cancel_query_on_cluster fails, so the disconnected query is never killed.
query_batch returns 404 for DashboardNotFound but 403 'You don't have access to this dashboard' for DashboardNotViewable, letting a caller tell private dashboard ids from nonexistent ones.

Targets that run outside ClickHouse (a connectionId / non-default executionTarget direct warehouse connection, or warehouse-native ExperimentQuery) are accepted, but disconnect cleanup only kills ClickHouse queries, so such work keeps running after the client leaves.
